TASK: The warehouse associate was picking bar stock from the third level of the material rack in stores. The task was routine scheduled work. Stage of the task: transport or handling material. Method in effect: SW-077 Material Rack Picking. The task was being performed as written. Equipment involved: Material rack MR-11 in the stores area, third level. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped and loaded or under tension. Equipment condition: known fault already reported. Detail: The rack has no end stops fitted on the third level, noted at the last rack inspection. The object handled weighed 25 to 50 lb. Handling difficulty: long - bar, pipe or sheet. It was held both hands. PPE in use: safety glasses, steel toe boots and cut resistant gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: The event was witnessed by at least one other person. Immediately before the event: standing square to the rack at the third level with both hands on a length of bar stock at about chest height, drawing it toward the body. Body position at the moment: reaching forward. At the moment of the event: the adjacent length rolled sideways as the first was withdrawn, travelled off the open end of the rack, and fell onto the left shoulder from the level above. Immediately after the event: the bar landed on the floor, the associate stepped back holding the left shoulder, and a coworker at the next aisle called the supervisor.

MECHANISM: Mechanism: A 6 foot length of steel bar stock rolled off the open end of the third rack level and fell onto the left shoulder, which was stationary. It travelled 1 to 3 feet. The object weighed 25 to 50 lb. Point of contact: top of the left shoulder. Force applied from above.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The third level had been loaded with mixed lengths that morning rather than the usual single size, so the lengths did not sit tight together. Conditions at the point of injury: poor or glaring lighting. Detail: The stores aisle is lit from the main bay and the upper rack levels sit in shadow. The event occurred in the first half of the shift. No overtime was being worked. It happened within the first few minutes. The warehouse associate had performed this task before. A known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. Detail: The missing end stops on rack MR-11 were raised at the last rack inspection and the action to fit them is still open. A guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Detail: End stops are the specified control for preventing material rolling off the rack and none are fitted on the third level. Stop-work opportunity: The pick could have been stopped once the mixed lengths were seen, but loading mixed lengths is common and was not treated as a hazard.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: At the scene, a cold pack was applied. This was given by a trained first aid responder. Notified: the supervisor and EHS. This happened within a few minutes. Afterwards, the area was barriered off. Work at the location stopped. The warehouse associate was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
